item.research_question: How do semi-coherent phase boundaries and the proportion of FCC/BCC phases influence the strengthening mechanism and mechanical properties in a eutectic dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and AlCoCrFeNi2.4 (eutectic dual-phase HEA with BCC and FCC lamellar phases)
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting of pure elements (Al, Co, Ni, Cr, Fe) at 1773 K, repeated melting at least five times with electromagnetic stirring, and solidification in a water-cooled copper hearth; some samples were cold rolled for pre-straining.
item.test_conditions: In situ tensile tests inside a TEM at a strain rate of ~1.0 μm∙s−1 with 200 kV accelerating voltage; room-temperature tensile tests using an Instron 5569 machine at a strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1.
key_findings: Decreasing the proportion of the hard BCC phase increased the overall strength due to potent impediments from chemically disordered semi-coherent phase boundaries.
The as-casted sample exhibited a fracture strength of ~0.94 GPa and ductility of ~25%.
Pre-straining the alloy increased the yield strength by a factor of ~5.
Increasing the volume fraction of BCC phase from 0.3 (Ni2.4) to 0.45 (Ni2.1) decreased the ultimate strength from 0.86 GPa to 0.97 GPa.
Dense dislocation walls formed along phase boundaries within the FCC phase, acting as strong barriers to dislocation motion.
The orientation relationship between phases was identified as (1–11)FCC//(01–1)BCC and [011]FCC//[111]BCC (K-S relationship).
A narrow segregation zone of randomly distributed Cr atoms, typically less than 2 nm in width, was detected near the phase boundary.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that semi-coherent phase boundaries decorated with chemically disordered multiple elements act as potent obstacles, causing dense dislocation storage in the FCC phase. This, combined with massive cross-slip and the formation of dislocation substructures (walls and networks) in the FCC phase, leads to exceptional work hardening and strength, making the FCC phase the primary contributor to strengthening rather than just the hard BCC phase.
item.limitations: The authors note that a critical limit presumably exists in the proportion of two phases, beyond which the overall strength would decrease with more FCC phases due to the failure of second phase strengthening.
item.future_work: The authors propose that their findings shed light on new ways to optimize mechanical properties by tuning the proportion of pre-strained FCC phases and leveraging the unique deformation mechanisms of dual-phase HEAs.
quotes: decreasing the proportion of BCC phase in fact increased the strength due to the existence of chemically disordered semi-coherent phase boundaries
the interaction between primary slip arrays and cross-slip systems during deformation increased the rate of dislocation accumulation by forming dislocation substructures
dense dislocation walls formed along the phase boundaries within the FCC phase, indicating that the FCC and BCC phase boundaries acted as strong barriers for dislocation motion
